author: Diego Sandoval
title: Jazz Chisholm Jr. (toe) has X-Rays come back negative
desc: Jazz Chisholm Jr.'s X-Rays on his right big toe came back negative, and he will be reassessed on Monday.
impact: Chisholm left Sunday's game against the Twins early, and the reasoning has been revealed as right big toe discomfort. The first round of tests is an encouraging sign, but the true extent of the injury will not be known until Monday.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Enrique Hernandez (oblique) takes BP Sunday
desc: Enrique Hernandez took batting practice on Sunday.
impact: Hernandez stepped into the batters box against Edwin Diaz. He continues to progress, but remains without a clear timetable to return.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Edwin Diaz (elbow) faces live hitters Sunday
desc: Edwin Diaz threw live batting practice on Sunday.
impact: Diaz came away from his live BP session encouraged with his stuff. He remains hopeful to be activated shortly after the All-Star break.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Shohei Ohtani (bicep) back in lineup Sunday
desc: Shohei Ohtani is back in the Dodgers lineup on Sunday against the Padres.
impact: Ohtani returns from a one-game absence. He returns to the top of the lineup.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Martin Perez exits early Sunday
desc: Martin Perez exited Sunday's game early after his left forearm was hit on a comebacker by Juan Soto.
impact: Perez will head to be further evaluated. There will be an update provided when available.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Cade Cavalli departs early Sunday
desc: Nationals right-hander Cade Cavalli departed Sunday's start against the Pirates with an undisclosed injury.
impact: Cavalli lasted just 2 1/3 innings on Sunday, allowing four runs (three earned) on six hits and two walks while striking out three. The injury-shortened outing comes on the heels of a 13-strikeout effort across seven shutout innings in his previous start against the Red Sox in Boston. An update on Cavalli's status should be available later on Sunday.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Byron Buxton dealing with reaggravated hip issue
desc: Twins outfielder Byron Buxton departed Sunday's game against the Yankees after re-aggravating a hip injury.
impact: The hip issue sidelined Buxton for nearly a week, but he returned to go 1-for-4 with a double, two RBI, and a run scored on Saturday. He removed himself from the game on Sunday after re-injuring his hip when he was caught stealing second base in the first inning. At this point, an injured-list stint could be a real possibility.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Brenton Doyle (oblique/groin) returned from rehab, remains on IL
desc: The Rockies have returned outfielder Brenton Doyle (oblique/groin) from his rehab assignment, and he will remain on the 10-day injured list.
impact: Doyle hit a home run in the resumption of his rehab assignment on Friday, but left groin tightness cropped up on Saturday, forcing his removal from a rehab game. The 28-year-old hit just .207 with one homer and nine stolen bases in 43 games prior to hitting the shelf and remains without a timetable to return.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Josh Jung dealing with sore knee
desc: Rangers third baseman Josh Jung is dealing with a sore knee, explaining his absence from Sunday's lineup.
impact: Jung fouled a ball off his knee on Saturday and came into the facility sore on Sunday. He is under evaluation with an update likely available in the next 24 hours.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Michael McGreevy pushed back to Tuesday versus Brewers
desc: Cardinals right-hander Michael McGreevy will start one of the two doubleheader games on Tuesday against the Brewers.
impact: The Cardinals announced Dustin May as Monday's starter for the series opener against the Brewers, pushing McGreevy back to one of the doubleheader games on Tuesday. McGreevy has been excellent with a 3.12 ERA in 17 starts this season, but a tiny 15.9% K% alongside a 5.58 xERA, 4.13 xFIP, and a 4.53 SIERA suggest he has been fortunate to post that surface ERA.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Dustin May to start Monday versus Brewers
desc: Cardinals right-hander Dustin May is scheduled to start Monday's game against the Brewers.
impact: May was hit on the ankle by a line drive in his last start on Thursday, but appears good to go for Monday's series opener against the rival Brewers. The right-hander has posted a 4.80 ERA across 16 starts this season, although his 3.89 xFIP and 3.94 SIERA suggest he is due for some better fortunes moving forward.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Jaden Hill (shoulder) to throw bullpen session Sunday
desc: Rockies right-hander Jaden Hill (shoulder) will throw his first bullpen session on Sunday.
impact: Hill, sidelined since June 24 with right shoulder tendinitis, has played catch recently, but has now progressed to throwing a bullpen session. The 26-year-old has posted a 5.06 ERA across 32 appearances for the Rockies this season.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Jeremy Pena (calf) to play in rehab games this week
desc: Astros shortstop Jeremy Pena (calf) is on track to play rehab games this week, with the hope of rejoining the team next weekend, according to manager Joe Espada.
impact: Espada believes Pena will be good to go for next weekend's series in Texas, which aligns with the hope Pena would need just the minimum time on the injured list. The 28-year-old has been enjoying another nice season when healthy, hitting .295 with six homers, eight stolen bases, and a .799 OPS across 48 games.
